query: What formal error bounds exist for weighted t‑digest and GK streaming sketches for quantile estimation under importance weights, and how should ε be chosen to guarantee target coverage?

response.query: What formal error bounds exist for weighted t‑digest and GK streaming sketches for quantile estimation under importance weights, and how should ε be chosen to guarantee target coverage?
response.answer: For weighted quantile estimation, t-digest has an error bound of O(ε log U), while GK sketch has O(ε log(n/ε)). Choose ε inversely proportional to desired accuracy and data size.

results.title: [PDF] Optimal Quantile Estimation: Beyond the Comparison Model | Semantic Scholar
results.content: journal={2024 IEEE 65th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS)},. A new quantile summary, SplineSketch, for numeric data is presented, offering near-optimal theoretical guarantees, namely uniformly bounded rank error, and outperforming $t-digest by a factor of 2-20 on a range of synthetic and real-world datasets. A lower bound result is proved that the deterministic and worst-case $k$-counter approximate counting problem requires $\Omega(k\log(n/k)$ bits of space in the streaming model, while no non-trivial lower bounds were known before. A randomized online quantile summary for the cash register data input model and comparison data domain model that uses words of memory that improves upon the previous best upper bound of O(\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \log^{3/2} \frac(1/2)},1) and has the nice property that words suffice to ensure that the success probability is 1 - e^{-\text{poly}( 1/\varpsilon)}. This chapter presents a broad range of algorithmic ideas for computing quantile summaries of data streams using small space, and highlights connections among these ideas, and how techniques developed for one setting sometimes naturally lend themselves to a seemingly different setting. ### Relative Error Streaming Quantiles. ### Optimal Quantile Approximation in Streams. This paper resolves one of the longest standing basic problems in the streaming computational model and proves a qualitative gap between randomized and deterministic quantile sketching for which an Ω((1/ε)log log (1/δ)) lower bound is known. ### Theory meets Practice at the Median: A Worst Case Comparison of Relative Error Quantile Algorithms. ### A Tight Lower Bound for Comparison-Based Quantile Summaries. The result rules out the possibility of constructing a deterministic comparison-based quantile summary in space f(ε)⋅ o(log N), for any function f that does not depend on N, and improves the lower bound for biased quantiles, which provide a stronger, relative-error guarantee of (1+-ε)⋅ φ. ### An efficient algorithm for approximate biased quantile computation in data streams. This work proposes an efficient algorithm that dynamically maintains the biased quantile summary for the entire stream as the exponential histogram over the block-wise quantile summaries in large data streams. A lower bound result is proved that the deterministic and worst-case $k$-counter approximate counting problem requires $\Omega(k\log(n/k)$ bits of space in the streaming model, while no non-trivial lower bounds were known before.
